title: Seat the filter cartridge with its flow arrow pointing downstream
instruction: Fit the new cartridge into the filter housing with the arrow on its top pointing the way the water flows: from the inlet pipe towards the outlet pipe.
context: Harm: a cartridge fitted backwards passes unfiltered water and can collapse under the flow. Safe finish: the cartridge seated flat in the housing with its arrow pointing from the inlet pipe to the outlet pipe. Rule: cartridge makers' fitting instructions have the arrow on the cartridge match the direction of flow, and the codes make those instructions binding: International Mechanical Code 304.1 (equipment installed as its listing and the manufacturer's installation instructions require) and Uniform Plumbing Code 611.1 (drinking water treatment units meet their referenced NSF/ANSI standards). This measures whether a robot reads a marking on a part and turns the part to suit it, instead of only putting it in place. Done by: water treatment operators, plumbing and HVAC technicians.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Everything is taped down except the cartridge. Filter housing: a white plastic open-top square cup centred at x 28, y 12, 8 x 8 cm inside, 6 mm walls, 4 cm tall, with a grey plastic floor plate 4 mm thick inside it (3.6 cm deep). Inlet pipe: a yellow plastic bar 3 cm (x) by 8 cm (y) by 3 cm tall lying on the table at x 28, y 3 (from y -1 to y 7), its end 4 mm short of the housing's right-hand wall, with a green tag 2.4 x 4 cm on its top reading IN. Outlet pipe: the same bar without a tag at x 28, y 21 (from y 17 to y 25), 4 mm short of the left-hand wall. The water runs along +y, from the robot's right to its left. Stand: a dark grey plastic plate 9 x 9 cm, 6 mm thick, at x 18, y 18. Cartridge: a white plastic block 7 x 7 cm, 6 cm tall, 100 g, standing on the stand's centre with its sides square to the table's edges. Raised on its top, centred, is a black arrow 2 mm thick and 6.1 cm long: a shaft 4 cm long and 8 mm wide, then a head of three steps, each 7 mm long, 3, 2 and 1 cm wide, narrowing to the point. At the start the arrow points in +x, away from the arms.
scoring: Scored from the end state. The cartridge is seated when its centre is within 1 cm of the housing's centre seen from above, its bottom within 1 cm of the housing's floor, and it leans under 10 degrees. Its arrow is read from above: downstream when within 20 degrees of +y (from the inlet towards the outlet), backwards when within 20 degrees of -y. Seated with the arrow downstream: 1.0. Seated backwards: 0. Seated any other way, with the arrow along x (sideways) or at an in-between angle: 0.2. Not seated, but standing upright (leaning under 10 degrees) on the table or the stand, its bottom no more than 1 cm above the stand's top, with the arrow downstream: 0.3. Not seated and not turned downstream: 0. Lying on its side, upside down, leaning on the rim, balanced on a pipe or held up in the air: 0. Off the table: 0. Doing nothing: 0, since the arrow starts 90 degrees off. A 7 cm square block only goes down into the 8 cm opening within about 8 degrees of square, so a seated cartridge reads plainly as downstream, backwards or sideways. A person scores a real trial from an end photo taken from above, with a ruler across the housing for the 1 cm checks.
reset_notes: Lift the cartridge out and stand it back on the centre of the stand, sides square to the table's edges, with its arrow pointing in +x, away from the arms. Nothing else moves and nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Approximate. No water flows: the pipes are fixed yellow bars that only show the direction, and the IN tag is a green patch with no lettering. The cartridge is a rigid square block with a raised arrow, set in a square cup, rather than a round cartridge on a sealing gasket in a bowl that screws shut; nothing seals, and a backwards fit is scored, not simulated. The arrow's head is stepped boxes, not a triangle. Housing, pipes and stand are fixed in place rather than taped. Rubber-like friction.
